paragraphs: Low-rank training reduces the computational and storage demands of neural networks by using restricted representations of their weights. However, changing the representation also changes the geometry of the optimization problem. This paper examines potential difficulties that arise when familiar momentum-based optimizers, including heavy ball methods and Adam, are used with these parameterizations.

The central finding is that classical momentum methods can struggle to reach a local optimum because of this geometry. The authors develop alternative training strategies using dynamical low-rank approximation, combining its treatment of constrained representations with momentum-based optimization. The resulting optimizers explicitly account for the structure of the parameter space when determining how training should progress.

Numerical experiments show faster convergence and stronger validation results at fixed parameter budgets. These findings suggest that the benefits of low-rank training depend partly on matching the optimizer to the representation being trained. The contribution is both an analysis of a potential failure mode and a geometrically motivated approach that performs better in the reported experiments.
neurips-2025-a-geometric-framework-for-m.tldr: Geometry-aware momentum optimizers improve convergence and validation results in the paper’s low-rank training experiments.

paragraphs: Many jailbreak methods optimize for an affirmative opening to a model’s response. This paper argues that such a fixed objective can constrain the behavior an attack produces: the response may be incomplete or unrealistic, and the prescribed wording can make optimization harder. The opening phrase therefore influences both attack effectiveness and what an evaluation reveals about safety.

AdvPrefix replaces that fixed objective with one or more prefixes selected for the particular model. Selection combines two criteria: how successfully a prefix elicits the targeted behavior when supplied as an initial response, and how likely the model considers that prefix. The objective is designed to fit into existing jailbreak methods, allowing their optimization target to change without replacing the broader attack.

In the reported example, changing GCG’s default prefixes on Llama-3 raises nuanced attack success from 14% to 80%. This supports the authors’ finding that the tested safety alignment does not generalize adequately to new prefixes. The result also shows why evaluations tied to a narrow response format can overlook substantial differences in vulnerability.
neurips-2025-advprefix-an-objective-for-.tldr: AdvPrefix changes the response-prefix objective used by jailbreak attacks, exposing substantially greater vulnerability in the reported Llama-3 test.

paragraphs: An interactive language-model assistant can ask questions before making a prediction, but useful interaction requires choosing questions that resolve uncertainty efficiently. Information Pursuit does this greedily, selecting the next question expected to provide the most information. Its effectiveness depends on uncertainty estimates, which can be distorted when a language model is excessively confident or insufficiently confident.

Conformal Information Pursuit replaces direct reliance on those probability-based estimates with uncertainty estimates derived from conformal prediction sets. These sets represent collections of possible answers. The method uses a relationship between conditional entropy and the average size of these sets to guide sequential questioning. The authors find this distribution-free representation of uncertainty more robust for the task.

On 20 Questions, the method improves predictive performance while shortening question-and-answer sequences relative to earlier Information Pursuit and uncertainty-based chain-of-thought approaches. On MediQ, an interactive doctor–patient task, it achieves competitive performance with direct single-turn prediction and offers greater interpretability. The findings support choosing questions through calibrated sets of possibilities rather than depending solely on the model’s raw confidence.
neurips-2025-conformal-information-pursu.tldr: Conformal Information Pursuit uses prediction-set sizes to select informative questions, improving accuracy and shortening interactions in 20 Questions.

paragraphs: Photorealistic Codec Avatars use generative models to render detailed human faces for virtual reality communication. Their computational demands make them difficult to run in real time on head-mounted devices, where processing delay and power efficiency matter. ESCA addresses this deployment problem by coordinating changes to model execution with a purpose-built hardware design.

The algorithmic component is a post-training quantization method tailored to Codec Avatar models. It enables computation at lower numerical precision while preserving output quality. The hardware component is a custom accelerator designed for integration into a virtual reality device’s system-on-chip. Together, these components form a framework for accelerating avatar inference on resource-constrained devices.

The experiments report improvements of up to 0.39 in FovVideoVDP quality score over the best 4-bit baseline and up to a 3.36-fold reduction in latency. End-to-end tests sustain 100 rendered frames per second. These results demonstrate the feasibility of high-fidelity avatar rendering under the tested edge-device conditions, with both visual quality and real-time execution considered in the design.
neurips-2025-esca-enabling-seamless-code.tldr: ESCA combines tailored low-precision computation with custom hardware to render high-fidelity codec avatars at 100 frames per second in end-to-end tests.

paragraphs: Fairness corrections can reduce overall model performance, particularly when the same correction is applied indiscriminately. FairNet instead makes correction conditional on the individual input. A bias detector identifies instances that need intervention, and a low-rank adaptation module activates selectively. This design aims to improve biased predictions while preserving performance on inputs that do not need correction.

The correction module is trained with a contrastive loss that reduces representation differences between sensitive groups within the same class. This targets minority-group underfitting while retaining the distinction between classes. The framework also accommodates complete, partial, or absent sensitive-attribute labels, addressing settings where those annotations are unavailable for some or all examples.

The theoretical result is conditional: with moderate true-positive and false-positive rates for the bias detector, FairNet can improve the worst-performing group without reducing overall performance, and may slightly improve it. Evaluations across vision and language benchmarks support the framework’s effectiveness. The detector’s behavior is therefore central to the stated guarantee, alongside the quality of the learned correction.
neurips-2025-fairnet-dynamic-fairness-co.tldr: FairNet selectively corrects detected bias, with conditional theoretical support for improving the worst group without sacrificing overall performance.

paragraphs: Foundation models learn different representations because their training data and objectives differ. A downstream task may therefore benefit from information distributed across several models or layers. ComBo addresses the challenge of combining that information efficiently, using frozen backbone models rather than requiring training updates to pass through each large model.

The adapter compresses layer activations into compact representations for individual tokens, then uses a lightweight transformer to make task-specific predictions. It requires neither dataset-specific hyperparameter tuning nor backpropagation through the backbones. A related mechanism evaluates each backbone’s relevance through joint probing, allowing selective adaptation when some models contribute more useful information than others.

Across the 19 VTAB-1k tasks, ComBo outperforms previous probing methods and matches or exceeds more expensive alternatives, including distillation-based model merging. It also supports efficient probing of tuned models. These results indicate that combining representations can be practical without updating every source model, and that selecting relevant backbones can improve the value of the combination.
neurips-2025-fantastic-features-and-wher.tldr: ComBo efficiently combines frozen features from multiple models and layers, achieving strong results across 19 VTAB-1k tasks.

paragraphs: Algorithm configuration chooses an algorithm’s parameters using a collection of sampled problem instances. For example, the parameters of a SAT solver can be selected this way before it is applied to other instances. The theoretical question is why a configuration that works on the sampled problems should also perform well beyond that sample.

This paper studies widely used model-based configurators through algorithmic stability. That framework connects generalization to how sensitive a learning procedure is to changes in its input data. The authors derive an algorithm-dependent bound under assumptions they describe as mild. Because the bound depends on the configuration procedure, it addresses the behavior of the selection process itself.

The authors describe their result as the first generalization bound for a model closely approximating practical model-based configurators, to the best of their knowledge. Its contribution is a theoretical connection between realistic configuration procedures and generalization guarantees. The result applies under its assumptions and concerns the modeled configurator, providing a more direct theoretical account of practical configuration than a purely abstract selection problem.
neurips-2025-generalization-bounds-for-m.tldr: The paper derives a stability-based generalization bound for a model closely approximating practical model-based algorithm configurators.

paragraphs: Coordinating mobile robots requires deciding both who should perform each task and when it can happen. Different capabilities, travel times, and dependencies between tasks complicate those decisions. This paper introduces HM-MATAS, a model that makes allocation and scheduling decisions simultaneously while representing the differences among agents and the temporal constraints on their work.

A residual heterogeneous graph transformer processes a graph containing agent capabilities, travel times, and spatial and temporal constraints. Attention operates over both nodes and edges, and reinforcement learning trains the model. Training uses problems with 10 agents and 20 tasks; evaluation shows generalization to scenarios with as many as 40 agents and 200 tasks.

The reported comparisons show substantially more feasible task assignments with much less computation. Against classical heuristics, for example, the model assigns 164.10% more feasible tasks using 3.83% of their time. It also reports gains over metaheuristics and an exact solver, plus 20-fold to 250-fold speedups over prior graph-based methods. These results support fast, one-shot scheduling across the tested scales.
neurips-2025-heterogeneous-graph-transfo.tldr: HM-MATAS jointly assigns and schedules heterogeneous robots, generalizing to larger teams and producing more feasible assignments faster in reported comparisons.

paragraphs: Reconstructing reflective objects from images requires separating surface properties from lighting effects. Gaussian-splatting methods can attach material attributes to their scene primitives, but insufficient constraints can mix illumination effects into the inferred materials. MaterialRefGS addresses this problem by combining consistency across viewpoints with a more physically grounded representation of the surrounding illumination.

The method requires 2D Gaussians to produce consistent material maps across views during deferred shading. It also examines how image appearance changes between viewpoints to identify strongly reflective regions, using those regions to constrain reflection strength. A ray-tracing environment model built with 2D Gaussian Splatting handles indirect illumination associated with objects occluding one another.

These components tie material estimation to evidence from multiple images and to the way light interacts with the scene. On widely used benchmarks, the authors report faithful recovery of illumination and geometry and state-of-the-art rendering quality for novel views. The findings support their claim that consistent materials and richer environment modeling are important for learning accurate reflections in this representation.
neurips-2025-materialrefgs-reflective-ga.tldr: MaterialRefGS improves reflective Gaussian-splatting reconstructions through consistent material estimates across views and ray-traced environment illumination.

paragraphs: Evaluating a personal assistant’s memory requires more than presenting it with a conversation. The evaluator also needs questions whose correct answers reliably follow from the user’s messages. Constructing those question-and-answer pairs automatically is difficult, especially when generated factual content may contain hallucinations. MemSim targets this data-construction problem so memory mechanisms can be assessed more objectively.

The system is a Bayesian simulator that generates user messages together with reliable evaluation questions and answers. It introduces a Bayesian Relation Network and a causal generation mechanism to reduce the influence of language-model hallucinations on factual information. The aim is to keep the resulting material diverse and scalable while maintaining consistency between the messages and their associated answers.

Using MemSim, the authors create MemDaily, a dataset centered on daily-life scenarios, and conduct extensive experiments to assess the approach. They also provide a benchmark for comparing memory mechanisms in language-model agents. The contribution supplies both a method for producing evaluation material and a concrete dataset through which different approaches to assistant memory can be studied.
neurips-2025-memsim-a-bayesian-simulator.tldr: MemSim generates user messages and reliable question–answer pairs to benchmark personal-assistant memory through the MemDaily dataset.

paragraphs: Macro-actions group behavior across time, potentially reducing how many decisions a reinforcement-learning agent must make. Yet adding them can worsen exploration because it also enlarges the action space. If every macro-action is treated as an unrelated choice, the agent has more alternatives to investigate without using the relationships between their component behaviors.

This paper introduces a regularization term that uses relationships among actions and macro-actions to improve credit assignment. A similarity matrix is meta-learned alongside the policy, allowing learning to exploit connections between choices. The intended effect is to reduce the effective dimensionality of the action space, making exploration more efficient even when additional macro-actions are available.

Experiments in Atari games and StreetFighter II show significant improvements over Rainbow-DQN in every evaluated environment. The authors also demonstrate that learned macro-action similarities can transfer to other environments with similar dynamics. These findings suggest that the usefulness of temporal abstractions depends partly on how experience is shared among related actions, rather than simply on adding longer action sequences.
neurips-2025-meta-learning-how-to-share-.tldr: Learning similarities among actions and macro-actions improves credit assignment and exploration in the reported game environments.

paragraphs: Traditional federated learning assumes that clients cooperate toward a shared model and aligned objectives. This paper considers clients whose individual goals may differ from the collective goal. It introduces Multiplayer Federated Learning, which treats clients as strategic players and frames the learning objective around reaching an equilibrium among their respective utility functions.

The proposed algorithm, PEARL-SGD, lets each player perform local stochastic gradient updates independently and communicate with the others periodically. This retains the communication-saving idea of local computation while applying it to a setting with multiple interacting objectives. Progress is therefore assessed relative to equilibrium behavior, rather than solely by improvement in a shared global objective.

The theoretical analysis shows convergence to a neighborhood of equilibrium in the stochastic setting, with less communication than the algorithm’s non-local counterpart. Numerical experiments verify the theoretical findings. The neighborhood qualification matters: the stated result concerns approaching equilibrium, rather than exact convergence to it. The framework provides a way to study communication efficiency when federated participants have distinct incentives.
neurips-2025-multiplayer-federated-learn.tldr: PEARL-SGD reduces communication while approaching equilibrium in a federated-learning framework with clients pursuing individual objectives.

paragraphs: Using a language model to judge generated text offers an appealing route to scalable evaluation. This position paper argues that adoption has moved faster than scrutiny of whether those judgments are reliable and valid. Its concern is whether an evaluator measures the intended qualities consistently and meaningfully, rather than whether it can readily produce a score.

Drawing on measurement theory from the social sciences, the authors examine four assumptions: that model judges can substitute for human judgment, that they possess suitable evaluation capabilities, that they scale effectively, and that they are cost-effective. Each assumption is assessed against limitations of language models, model-based judging, and current practices for evaluating generated language.

The discussion is grounded in text summarization, data annotation, and safety alignment, covering several stages of the machine-learning pipeline. As a position paper, its contribution is a critical framework for examining evaluation practices rather than a universal empirical verdict against model judges. It calls for more responsible assessment so that increasingly common automated judgments support dependable progress in language generation.
neurips-2025-neither-valid-nor-reliable-.tldr: This position paper questions four assumptions behind language-model judges and argues for stronger scrutiny of their reliability and validity.

paragraphs: A web agent may recognize an image correctly yet struggle when solving a puzzle requires several coordinated decisions and interactions. CAPTCHAs expose this distinction and can prevent agents from completing automated web tasks. Open CaptchaWorld provides a web-based environment for studying these combined visual-reasoning and interaction demands in multimodal language-model agents.

The benchmark contains 225 puzzles covering 20 modern CAPTCHA types. Its proposed CAPTCHA Reasoning Depth metric describes the number of cognitive and motor steps needed to solve a puzzle. This adds a way to characterize the required sequence of reasoning and actions, beyond simply labeling the kind of visual challenge presented.

The experiments reveal a substantial gap between agents and humans. The highest reported agent success rate is 40.0%, achieved by Browser-Use Openai-o3, compared with 93.3% for humans. These results show that strong performance on static perception tasks does not establish comparable competence on this interactive benchmark. The platform offers a concrete setting for diagnosing where current agents struggle with multistep visual tasks.
neurips-2025-open-captchaworld-a-compreh.tldr: Open CaptchaWorld tests interactive visual reasoning with 225 CAPTCHAs, revealing a large performance gap between current agents and humans.

paragraphs: This paper studies how to tune auxiliary regression models when the ultimate goal is statistical inference. The target is Expected Conditional Covariance, which measures association between two variables after conditioning on covariates and is relevant to conditional independence testing and causal inference. Estimation requires nuisance functions describing how each variable relates to those covariates.

The analysis assumes linear regression models and a high-dimensional regime where the ratio of covariates to observations approaches a positive finite constant. Without further structure, nuisance functions cannot be consistently estimated in this regime. The authors develop bias corrections for three existing estimators using ridge-regression nuisance estimates and examine two sample-splitting strategies, obtaining square-root-n consistency for the corrected target estimates.

They then derive asymptotic variances to study how estimator choice, data splitting, and ridge tuning interact. A central finding is that tuning for the best nuisance-function predictions may not minimize the final estimator’s variance. Numerical experiments verify the theory, supporting the need to choose tuning parameters according to the eventual inferential objective.
neurips-2025-optimal-nuisance-function-t.tldr: Under proportional high-dimensional asymptotics, the best ridge tuning for prediction may differ from the best tuning for conditional-covariance inference.

paragraphs: Estimating a person’s 3D pose from a single image is difficult when the initial 2D joint predictions are inaccurate or parts of the body obscure one another. Directly mapping each predicted 2D joint to a 3D joint can carry those errors forward. PandaPose introduces a shared intermediate representation built around 3D anchors to address these problems.

Joint-specific anchors in a canonical coordinate system provide spatial priors, while depth-aware feature lifting adds depth information hierarchically to help resolve self-occlusion. A decoder combines the anchors with visual features and geometric depth cues. The resulting anchor queries support an ensemble prediction of joint locations, allowing the final pose to draw on several forms of evidence.

Experiments on Human3.6M, MPI-INF-3DHP, and 3DPW show advantages over existing approaches. On challenging Human3.6M conditions, the authors report a 14.7% error reduction relative to state-of-the-art methods, alongside qualitative evidence of robustness. The findings support using a structured 3D intermediate space to reduce dependence on potentially unreliable 2D pose estimates.
neurips-2025-pandapose-3d-human-pose-lif.tldr: PandaPose combines 3D joint anchors, visual evidence, and depth cues to improve single-image 3D pose estimation.

paragraphs: Cropping can improve the framing of a photograph, but it has limited ability to repair awkward relationships between subjects. Changing perspective alters how those subjects appear relative to one another without changing their actual positions. This paper develops photography perspective composition around that practice, aiming to help users find more aesthetically balanced views.

The authors address two obstacles: limited datasets showing perspective transformations and a lack of defined criteria for evaluating perspective quality. They introduce an automated dataset-building framework based on expert photographs and a video-generation approach that illustrates movement from less favorable views to improved ones. A perspective-quality assessment model based on human performance provides the evaluation component.

The approach requires no additional prompt instructions or camera trajectories. Its intended role is to guide ordinary users by showing how a change in viewpoint can improve composition. The contribution brings together training-data construction, visual demonstration, and quality assessment, making perspective adjustment a concrete computational task alongside the more established task of choosing a crop.
neurips-2025-photography-perspective-com.tldr: The paper develops data generation, transformation videos, and quality assessment to recommend more aesthetically pleasing photographic perspectives.

paragraphs: Private set union asks which items can be reported when each user contributes a bag of at most k items. Privacy makes rare items particularly difficult to release. The paper studies differentially private algorithms that report only items actually present, measuring utility as the expected number of distinct items they return.

Because achievable utility differs greatly across datasets, the authors introduce a utility ratio that compares performance with a dataset-specific upper bound and then considers the worst dataset. They give algorithms with guaranteed ratios and bounds on what is achievable. Although one algorithm can be optimal on every dataset when k equals one, they show this is impossible when users may contribute multiple items.

The paper also develops an algorithm that uses a prior prediction of item frequencies. When that prediction matches the actual histogram, it achieves maximum possible utility regardless of k. When it is imperfect, performance degrades gracefully with the largest absolute histogram error. This identifies both an unavoidable tradeoff for general datasets and a conditional benefit from accurate prior information.
neurips-2025-private-set-union-with-mult.tldr: Multiple contributions prevent universal instance-optimal private set union, but accurate predictions of item frequencies can recover maximum utility.

paragraphs: Differentially private estimation becomes difficult when data values are unbounded, because individual observations can have large effects on the result. Traditional solutions often require sensitivity analyses tailored to each statistical problem. This paper develops a more general framework that uses data truncation to control sensitivity while explicitly accounting for the distortion that truncation introduces.

The method combines tools from truncated statistics with maximum likelihood estimation and differentially private stochastic gradient descent. Truncation helps limit sensitivity, while the estimation procedure corrects the resulting bias. The authors construct computationally efficient estimators for exponential-family distributions, including estimation of Gaussian means and covariances, and obtain near-optimal sample complexity.

The stated scope extends beyond earlier exponential-family work limited to bounded or one-dimensional families. The analysis also establishes improved uniform convergence guarantees for exponential-family log-likelihood functions, a theoretical result that may have uses beyond this framework. Together, the results show how controlling extreme observations and correcting their statistical consequences can support a broader approach to private estimation.
neurips-2025-private-statistical-estimat.tldr: The paper combines truncation with bias correction to build efficient private estimators for unbounded exponential-family distributions.

paragraphs: Completing a 3D object from a partial observation requires inferring surfaces that are not visible in the input. Existing methods can struggle with consistency, computational cost, and sharp boundaries. RaySt3R approaches this task through novel-view prediction: it estimates what the object’s depth would look like from additional viewpoints, then combines those predictions into a complete shape.

The input is a single image containing both color and depth. A requested viewpoint is represented by query rays, and a feedforward transformer predicts depth, an object mask, and confidence for each corresponding pixel. Repeating this process for multiple views provides the predictions that the system fuses into a 3D reconstruction.

Evaluations on synthetic and real-world datasets show state-of-the-art performance, with improvements over the baselines on every tested dataset and gains of up to 44% in 3D Chamfer distance. These findings support the use of predicted depth views as an effective representation for shape completion. The method connects reconstruction to a view-based prediction task while also estimating object boundaries and prediction confidence.
neurips-2025-rayst3r-predicting-novel-de.tldr: RaySt3R completes objects from one RGB-D image by predicting and combining depth maps from additional viewpoints.

paragraphs: Generative video editing can give a scene new motion, but the resulting frames may contain inconsistent geometry, implausible movement, or missing structure behind occlusions. Those errors complicate reconstruction of a deforming 3D scene over time. Restage4D uses the unedited original video as additional supervision when reconstructing the scene from its edited counterpart.

A video-rewinding training scheme links the original and edited sequences through a shared motion representation. An occlusion-aware as-rigid-as-possible regularizer helps preserve local structure during deformation. A separate backtracing mechanism supplies missing geometry in the canonical representation when previously hidden regions become visible. These components allow structural evidence from the original sequence to support the newly animated scene.

Tests on DAVIS and PointOdyssey show improvements in geometric consistency, motion quality, and 3D tracking. The authors also report correction of errors introduced by generative models, including cases with hallucinated content or inconsistent motion. The key contribution is a reconstruction pipeline that uses the original scene’s evidence to preserve structure while accommodating edited motion.
neurips-2025-restage4d-reanimating-defor.tldr: Restage4D uses original-video supervision to preserve geometry and correct errors when reconstructing scenes with edited motion.

paragraphs: World models predict how environments evolve, allowing agents to consider the consequences of actions. SAMPO addresses problems in visual autoregressive world models involving spatial coherence, decoding cost, and motion representation. It combines generation across spatial scales within a frame with causal prediction across frames, treating spatial organization and temporal progression in complementary ways.

The model combines temporal causal decoding with bidirectional spatial attention, preserving locality while allowing parallel decoding within each scale. An asymmetric tokenizer retains spatial detail in observed frames and represents future-frame dynamics more compactly. A trajectory-aware motion prompt supplies information about object and robot movement, directing attention toward dynamic regions and improving temporal consistency and physical realism.

Experiments show competitive results in action-conditioned video prediction and model-based control, with improved generation quality and 4.4-fold faster inference. Evaluations also demonstrate generalization to unseen tasks and benefits from larger model sizes. The findings support coordinating spatial generation, temporal prediction, and explicit motion cues to produce efficient, visually coherent imagined sequences in the tested settings.
neurips-2025-sampo-scale-wise-autoregres.tldr: SAMPO combines generation across spatial scales with temporal modeling and trajectory cues, improving video quality with 4.4-fold faster inference.

paragraphs: Test-time adaptation updates a model using unlabeled incoming data so it can respond to changing data distributions. Frequent updates can be too costly for devices with limited resources. SNAP reduces how often adaptation occurs and how much data it uses, aiming to retain useful accuracy while lowering the delay associated with adaptation.

Its representative memory stores a small collection of examples selected to reflect both class and domain characteristics. These examples support adaptation when only a small portion of the stream is used. A second component adjusts normalization statistics during inference using the representative memory, helping align predictions with shifting target domains even between adaptation updates.

Integrated with five existing adaptation algorithms, SNAP maintains competitive accuracy when adapting from only 1% of incoming data. Across adaptation rates from 1% to 50%, the reported latency reduction reaches 93.12%, with accuracy drops below 3.3%. These results support sparse adaptation as a practical efficiency strategy for latency-sensitive edge applications, with representative memory helping preserve performance between infrequent updates.
neurips-2025-snap-low-latency-test-time-.tldr: SNAP uses representative memory and inference-time normalization to preserve competitive accuracy with sparse adaptation and substantially lower latency.

paragraphs: Learning with Errors is a mathematical problem important to post-quantum cryptography. Under certain parameter settings, AI-based attacks already rival or outperform classical approaches. Studying those methods is difficult for many AI researchers because generating suitable training data requires substantial computation, time, and specialist knowledge. TAPAS addresses that access barrier through ready-to-use datasets.

The datasets cover several Learning with Errors settings and are intended for prototyping new AI approaches to the problem. The paper documents how the data was created, establishes attack-performance baselines, and identifies directions for further research. These components give researchers both material for training and reference results for evaluating new approaches.

The contribution is research infrastructure for investigating AI-based cryptanalysis, rather than a claim that post-quantum cryptography is generally broken. The motivating comparison with classical attacks is explicitly restricted to certain parameter settings. By making data available off the shelf, TAPAS enables AI practitioners to investigate those settings without first reproducing the demanding data-generation process themselves.
neurips-2025-tapas-datasets-for-learning.tldr: TAPAS provides ready-to-use datasets and baselines for studying AI attacks on several Learning with Errors settings.

paragraphs: Object re-identification matches observations of the same object, but existing systems often specialize in particular sensing modalities or categories such as people or vehicles. Maintaining separate models for each retrieval task consumes training and deployment resources. This paper introduces a unified task in which one model handles retrieval across both different modalities and different object categories.

The proposed UPCL framework uses prototypes to address two sources of mismatch. Its modality-enhancement module employs modality-unbiased prototypes to improve both features shared across modalities and features formed by combining modalities. Its consistency regularizer clusters prototypes to guide discriminative learning with category-consistent information, addressing differences in category semantics alongside differences in modality distributions.

Together, the modules aim to learn useful shared and fused feature spaces while retaining strong category discrimination. Experiments on RGBNT201 and RGBNT100 report strong performance on the unified retrieval task. The contribution connects a broader task definition with a training framework designed for its specific challenges, supporting the use of one retrieval model across combinations that would otherwise require specialized systems.
neurips-2025-unbiased-prototype-consiste.tldr: UPCL uses modality-unbiased prototypes and category-consistency regularization to support multiple object re-identification tasks within one model.
